handoffs.notes: FuzeInfra#499/#500. Source is the hand-off Secret from #166/#183 (a single `password` key, unrotated since 2026-07-08). The consumer does not consume a bare password: mendys-prod/mendys-secrets holds a composed DATABASE_URL, so format is postgres-url. The re-seal that resolved #499 by hand (MendysRobotics#273) changed exactly this one encryptedData key and left the other 23 alone — which is why the publisher must kubeseal --merge-into and must never regenerate the manifest.

Added 2026-08-20 (FuzeInfra#610). Found by gate-handoff-coverage on its FIRST real run, not by the manual sweep in #609 — my local clone was stale and reported zero references; code search reads the default branch and found deploy/helm/fuzeagent/templates/ui.yaml consuming the token via secretKeyRef. PARTIALLY WIRED, deliberately: registration/README.md records that FuzeAgent is a multi-service deployment and exactly one deployment must run registration — wiring more than one would have them race and duplicate-register — so choosing the owner was left to devops-engineer. This entry does NOT make that choice; it only ensures the token EXISTS when it is made. Path matches this repo's convention: sealed manifests live in deploy/contabo/sealed/ (alongside ghcr-pull and fuzeagent-secrets), and the fuzeagent-sealed Argo Application already GitOps-applies that directory, so a new file there is picked up without further wiring. Created from scratch — no fuzefront-registration manifest exists in the repo today.

Added 2026-08-20 (FuzeInfra#610). CORRECTS AN EXCLUSION I MADE IN #609 ON A WRONG PREMISE. I excluded FuzeHub there saying its secret was a Helm TEMPLATE that `kubeseal --merge-into` would corrupt. That was inferred from the PATH — the file sits under helm/fuzehub/templates/ — and reading the file disproves it: fuzefront-registration-sealed.yaml contains NO template syntax at all. No {{ }}, no {{- if }} guard, a hardcoded `namespace: fuzehub`, and real ciphertext already in encryptedData.token. It is a static manifest that merely lives in templates/, so Helm passes it through unchanged and merge-into operates on it exactly as it does on the siblings. Reasoning from a filename instead of the artifact is the same mistake this registry keeps catching elsewhere; recorded so the exclusion is not reinstated from the path alone. Note the manifest is rendered as part of the chart, so the hardcoded namespace travels with it — pre-existing, and not changed here.
